candidate_spec.high_level_variant: Ego follows a similar route in Town01 with a crossing walker slightly closer to ego’s lane near the collision point, maintaining moderate speed and no braking despite valid waypoints and perceived objects.
candidate_spec.mutation_intent: Keep the original interaction type (ego vs. crossing walker) but move the walker slightly toward the lane and slightly adjust its speed so that a collision remains likely while preserving the Phase 1 pattern: ego in motion, perception/prediction objects present, unblocked final waypoints, and no braking before impact under an ambiguous actuation-command situation.
pre_execution_validation_rules: Ensure actor_index 0 remains a walker with autopilot navigation crossing or entering ego’s path within the final few seconds before the expected collision time.
Verify that ego’s planned route (mission) remains approximately aligned with the original (Town01, same road segment) so that the walker is in ego’s forward path.
Confirm that no aggressive braking or forced emergency-stop behaviors are injected by other scenario logic before the anticipated collision window.
Check that perception and prediction configurations are enabled so at least one object (the walker) is expected to appear in those topics near the crossing.
post_execution_validation_rules: Confirm that at least one collision involving ego is reported, occurring while ego speed is nonzero and does not significantly decrease in the 2–3 seconds prior to impact.
Verify that brake-related signals (vehicle_status and vehicle_cmd) remain near zero or show no significant braking in the critical window before collision.
Check that final_waypoints are present and unblocked (full waypoint count comparable to baseline) throughout the seconds before collision.
Confirm that perception and prediction topics contain at least one object close in time to the collision, consistent with the walker or other nearby agents.

Inspect vehicle_cmd vs vehicle_status for an ambiguous actuation pattern similar to the original (e.g., zeroed commands with nonzero speed/throttle, or otherwise inconsistent with the observed motion).
Treat any lane_invasion flags as optional and not required for considering the run consistent with the original root-cause pattern.
uncertainty: Exact internal controller behavior leading to zero braking cannot be enforced at scenario level; post-execution logs must be checked to see if the ambiguous vehicle_cmd vs vehicle_status mismatch is preserved.
The precise point of impact and which body part of the walker is hit are not controlled here and may vary, as long as a collision with ego occurs under motion and no braking.
Lane invasion status may differ from the original due to minor geometric shifts; this is acceptable and not required for root-cause preservation.
